profile.behavior: Usually remains low in dense cover, walking or climbing through vegetation and making short flights when flushed. Forages on mud, at water edges, and in shallow water, picking seeds and invertebrates from the ground, plants, or water surface. Males sing a simple trill from raised perches.
field_marks: Compact, robust sparrow with a moderately long, rounded tail
Short conical bill with a yellowish base
Rusty crown in breeding plumage; browner and streaked outside the breeding season
Gray face with a dark eye and dark line behind it; clean whitish throat
Rusty-chestnut wings and back marked with dark streaks
profile.habitat: Densely vegetated wetlands, especially freshwater marshes, sedge swamps, bogs, wet meadows, and brushy margins with cattails, reeds, grasses, or shrubs. Also uses brackish marshes; during migration and winter it may occur in damp thickets, streamside cover, and weedy fields.

findings: The primary specimen is a coherent single Swamp Sparrow with one head and bill, a naturally overlapped far wing, two correctly attached pinkish legs with plausible perching feet, and one moderately long graduated-to-rounded tail. No duplicated or malformed attached anatomy is present.

The detached wing and head are clearly intentional supplementary studies. The wing has plausible covert and flight-feather organization, while the study bill matches the primary bill in its short conical shape, dark upper mandible, yellowish lower base, and normal projection.

Species identity is convincing against the supplied photographs and direct source descriptions: compact robust sparrow proportions, rusty crown, gray face and nape, dark eyeline, whitish throat, reddish-brown wings, streaked upperparts, relatively long legs, and a rounded tail.

The principal plumage is consistent with an adult Swamp Sparrow. The rusty crown, gray facial pattern, pale throat, warm rufous wing coverts, and subdued underparts agree with the references; no unsupported seasonal rewrite is required.
The common name, scientific name, and family are correct: Swamp Sparrow, Melospiza georgiana, Passerellidae.

All three printed measurements exactly match the All About Birds values: length 12–15 cm (4.7–5.9 in), weight 15–23 g (0.5–0.8 oz), and wingspan 18–19 cm (7.1–7.5 in). Audubon's rounded ranges are compatible.
